minutes.headline: Open Space Committee voted to endorse the Pierce farm agricultural preservation restriction for the spring Town Meeting warrant.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a Lake Shirley Improvement Corporation representative ask about using a town-owned parcel for lake-resident recreation. what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee voted 5-0 to endorse the Chase Road / Northfield Road agricultural preservation restriction on the Pierce tree farm, including a town match.
The match is about ten percent of the acquisition price, with the state program providing most of the funding.
A Lake Shirley Improvement Corporation representative asked to use the town-owned lake parcel for resident recreation; members said exclusive use is not possible and public access is the aim.
The committee moved its next meeting from April 20 to April 13 and agreed to forward the minutes to the Board of Selectmen, particularly on the Pierce APR.
Bob will raise the unclear title of the Oliver lot with town counsel, and the chair will look for guidance on owner-unknown parcels.

why_it_matters: The endorsed town match toward the Pierce restriction is the kind of appropriation residents are asked to approve at Town Meeting, so the committee's vote is a step toward a warrant article.
The Lake Shirley discussion touches what the town pays for at the dam house and who may use town-owned land on the lake, a question of public access versus a resident group's use.
watch_next: The Pierce agricultural preservation restriction on the spring Town Meeting warrant, and the Board of Selectmen's handling of the forwarded minutes.
The next Open Space Committee meeting on April 13, with a speaker on the West Street and Pleasant Street parcels.
